title: fix: use f64 arithmetic for zoom focal point calculation

## Summary

Fixes the magnifier viewport calculation for **Centered** and **OnEdge** cursor tracking modes at zoom levels other than 2x.

**Root cause:** The focal point scale factor was computed using integer division (`i32 / i32`), which truncates when the result isn't an exact integer. The divisor is `output_width - zoomed_width` (where `zoomed_width = output_width / level`). At 2x zoom this happened to work (e.g. `1920 / (1920 - 960) = 2`), but at 3x: `1920 / (1920 - 640) = 1` instead of the correct `1.5`. With fractional display scaling (e.g. 175%), odd logical output dimensions cause truncation at even lower zoom levels.

A second bug in `OutputZoomState::new()` used `.upscale(level)` instead of the correct `.upscale(level / (level - 1.0))` for the initial Centered focal point — also only correct at exactly 2x (where `level == level / (level - 1.0)`).

## Changes

- `OutputZoomState::new()` Centered branch: correct the scale factor from `level` to `level / (level - 1.0)`
- `update_focal_point()` OnEdge branch: replace integer division with f64 division
- `update_focal_point()` Centered branch: compute focal point directly from f64 cursor position, eliminating i32 intermediate conversions

## Test plan

- [x] Tested with Centered cursor tracking at 125%, 150%, 175%, 200%, 250%, 300% zoom on a 175% HiDPI display
- [x] Verified cursor stays centered in viewport (previously drifted at all levels except 200%)
- [x] Verified OnEdge mode still works correctly
- [x] Verified Continuously mode unaffected (it doesn't use this code path)
- [x] `cargo check` passes

## Note

After this fix, a small residual cursor jitter remains visible in Centered mode (cursor briefly glitches off-center, even during slow movement). This appears to be a separate issue in the rendering pipeline, not related to the focal point calculation fixed here. The focal point itself is now mathematically correct.

Closes #1503
